To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the Sobel test is an asymptotic test of the indirect effect that is robust to violations of normality; (2) the Sobel confidence interval is a robust confidence interval for the indirect effect that performs well even when the indirect effect is not normally distributed; (3) the percentile bootstrap confidence interval is a non-parametric confidence interval that performs well even in the presence of non-normality; (4) the bootstrap test of the indirect effects is robust to violations in normality and
the three approaches to assessing indirect effects in multiple mediation are the asymptotic approach, the resampling approach, and the bootstrapping approach.

(1) multiple mediation is an important and common phenomenon in behavioral research, (2) the use of multiple mediators can be used to assess the relative importance of mediators in the same model, and (3) the three approaches to assessing multiple mediators that we describe are complementary in their use and can be used to address a variety of research questions.
